one_month_reasoning: The window (to 2026-11-08) almost certainly contains Q3-2026 earnings. Paycom reported Q3-2025 on Nov 5 and Q2-2026 on Aug 5, so early November is likely, but the date is unconfirmed at the time of writing. Earnings-day moves have been large: -10.7% (Nov 2025), +0.9% close but -12% intraday (Feb 2026, guidance miss), +9.6% (May 2026) and +23.6% (Aug 2026). That puts the monthly sigma near 15.5%, above the 46%/3.5 = 13% rule. My lean is slightly negative, not a call. The FY26 guide implies H2 revenue growth of ~6% against Q2's 9.8%. Q4 comps are tough. The stock is up ~60% since late July, above the $220 consensus target, with BofA initiating at Sell on Sep 29. Last year's Q3 print fell 10.7%. Against that, management has beaten and raised twice this year, and buybacks support the shares (~$1.66B authorization left). The founder's new 10b5-1 sales cannot start before Dec 1. I use a median of ~$231 (-0.5%) with a 15.5% sigma, so P(>= $232.22) = 0.49.

fair_value.method: 60% P/E: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ~$15.02 (FY27 consensus $13.97 rolled forward at +10%) x 16x, inside the 12-peer range and just below its 17.1x median = $240. 40% DCF: normalized unlevered FCF $690M, 9% WACC, 2.5% terminal = $245. Blend $242.0, ~4% above $232.22.

inputs_detail.derivation: 13.97 x 1.10. 10% = consensus FY27 revenue growth 7.44% + ~2% net share shrink from continuing buybacks ($1.66B authorization, FCF >$650M) + small margin gain, less a float-interest headwind if rates fall (interest on client funds ~$105M FY26 guide, Q2 $26.0M). Deliberately below the 15.45% FY27 consensus step-up, which is inflated by the full-year effect of the 10.9M shares bought in H1-2026.

Peer median forward P/E 17.1x (range 7.6x-23.0x, 12 peers). 16x sits inside the range, a little below the median: PAYC's revenue growth (7.4% FY27 consensus) is only slightly above the peer median (~6.4%), and its above-peer EPS growth comes mostly from debt-funded buybacks (non-organic, and capped by leverage). Float income that falls with rates, founder share sales and the AI seat-count risk also argue against paying above the median. PAYC trades at 17.68x today (StockAnalysis), or 16.6x FY27 consensus ($232.22/13.97).

bear.story: Recurring growth slows to ~5% in 2027 as AI-driven headcount cuts at clients shrink per-employee billing. The new sales hires ramp slowly, the up-market push stalls (BofA thesis) and retention slips below 90%. Rate cuts cut float income (~$105M/yr). FY27 EPS comes in ~$13.0-13.5 (well under the $13.97 consensus) and the multiple de-rates to ~12x, near INTU and ASUR. Founder sales of up to 1.09M shares (Dec-26 to Jun-27) add supply. Shares revisit $155-165, the pre-Q2-print level.

base.story: Revenue grows ~7% and EBITDA margin holds at ~46%. Buybacks shrink the share count ~2%/yr. FY27 EPS lands near $13.9 and NTM EPS reaches ~$15 by Oct-27. The P/E holds at ~16x, in line with payroll peers (PAYX 17.2x, PCTY 17.6x). The stock is roughly flat to +5%, giving back none of the rerating but adding little.

bull.story: New products (IWant AI, asset management, succession) and the larger sales force push recurring growth back to 9-10%. Cost automation lifts margins toward 48-50%. Debt-funded buybacks keep shrinking the count and FY28 EPS reaches ~$16+. The multiple expands to ~19-20x, near ADP/TYL, for ~$310.

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 16.0x NTM EPS at the horizon, inside the range and ~1x below the 17.1x median. PAYC today: 17.68x forward (StockAnalysis), 16.6x FY27 consensus; TTM EV/EBITDA 15.06x vs 14.2x peer median. On FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance ($1.007-1.022B) EV/EBITDA is ~10.9x, but that basis is not comparable to the TTM GAAP peer column.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium is applied. PAYC's above-peer EPS growth (15.5% vs ~12% median) is mostly financial engineering: 10.9M shares (~20%) retired in H1-26 for $1.42B, partly with $900M of revolver debt. That boost does not persist at the same rate. Organic revenue growth (7.4% FY27 consensus; H2-26 implied ~6%) is only modestly above the payroll peer median, and revenue retention (91%) is ordinary. The small discount to the median reflects three things that last through the horizon: rate-sensitive float income (~5% of revenue at ~100% margin), seat-based pricing exposed to AI headcount reduction at clients (Paycom itself cut ~500 roles for AI automation), and a founder selling plan. Being inside the peer range, it needs no claim of structural under-performance.

thesis_break_reason: $165 is ~11.8x FY27 consensus EPS ($13.97) and roughly the pre-Q2-print price ($174.80 on Aug 5, 2026). Trading there would most likely mean the 2026 margin and growth reset has failed: a FY27 guide below ~5% revenue growth, retention falling, or an EBITDA guide cut. It would no longer look like ordinary volatility in a 46%-vol stock. Leverage would also bite more: net debt is ~0.7x EBITDA now, covenants are max 3.5x leverage and min 3.0x interest coverage, so there is no covenant risk at that level, but buyback capacity would shrink.

reasoning:
Skeptic lane. Q2-26 was strong (revenue +9.8%, adj. EBITDA margin 44.2%, non-GAAP EPS $2.78 vs $2.06), and the stock rerated from ~$145 in late July to $232. The bear evidence:
(1) Quality of the beat. Margin came largely from cutting total R&D spend ($111.7M -> $67.6M in Q2) and headcount, not from faster growth. Guidance implies H2 revenue growth of only ~6%.
(2) Financial engineering. 10.9M shares (~20%) were retired in H1 for $1.42B, funded partly by a $900M secured revolver. Equity fell to $572M. Consensus FY27 EPS growth of 15.5% is flattered by that share-count shrink.
(3) FCF quality. The >$650M FY26 FCF guide includes a ~$75M one-off tax receivable unwind. Capex and capitalized R&D are also down sharply. Server useful lives went from 3 to 6 years in Q3-25, called immaterial so far.
(4) Sentiment and holders. Consensus is Hold with a $220 target, below the price. BofA initiated at Sell ($200) on Sep 29. The founder's Ernest Group filed a new 10b5-1 plan for up to 1.09M shares from Dec 1 (the Dec-25 plan sold nothing, so price limits likely matter). Short interest is moderate (~2.6M shares, ~5.7% of shares out).
(5) Rate-sensitive float income.
Weighing it honestly: credit risk is low (net debt ~0.7x EBITDA vs a 3.5x covenant). No material litigation is disclosed. Retention is steady at 91%. The stock's 16.6x FY27 P/E already sits at the payroll-peer median, so the bear case is mostly priced as 'no premium', not as a fraud or collapse.
Valuation: 60% P/E ($240) and 40% DCF ($245) give $242, ~4% upside, under a 7-8% cost of equity.
Distribution: median ~$234 with sigma ~0.39 (below the 46% realized vol, which includes the Feb panic). The left tail is fattened for leverage, AI seat risk and founder supply: P(<$163) ~18.5%, consistent with a 25% bear case centred at $160.
Research limits: Twelve Data statistics, price-target and insider endpoints were plan-restricted. Q3 date not confirmed. Peer EV/EBITDA is TTM, not forward. The mandated 12-peer comps need 24 data pages, which pulls the in-lane share of all sources to ~33%; of the 22 non-comps sources, 15 (68%) are in-lane (credit documents, 13D/A 10b5-1 plans, Form 4, short interest, sell-side Sell/Hold ratings, critical press, fund-letter detractor note).
